text:
B: Hi, yeah, can you hear me alright?
A: yeah, can hear you fine
B: Good. I'm Gareth. You're Liam, is it?
A: Yeah. Liam.
B: Right. Er, so where are you calling from?
A: Walsall. Bloxwich, sort of.
B: Oh right, Midlands. I'm Maidstone, in Kent. You look like you've had a long day, if you don't mind me saying.
A: Yeah, er, just come off nights. Did four on the bounce. Bit knackered, to be honest.
B: What's the job?
A: IT technician at a parcel depot, up by junction ten on the M6. I keep the scanners going, the label printers, the PCs on the sort lines, the Wi-Fi. Anything with a plug, really, they ring me.
B: Ha, right. I said on the form you looked like you worked somewhere like mine, but I think that was the fleece.
A: What do you do then?
B: Civil engineer. Drainage, flood risk mainly. So if a culvert collapses, or a developer wants to build on a flood plain, that's sort of me. Bit of office, bit of home, bit of standing in a field in the rain in a hi-vis.
A: Right. So pipes and that.
B: Pipes and that, yeah. Bigger pipes. What's the worst one you've had, on nights?
A: Er... Black Friday last year, a whole sorter line went down about three in the morning. Switch had died in the cabinet. Thousands of parcels backing up, managers all running round.
B: What did you do?
A: Just swapped it. Had a spare. Took about twenty minutes. I let them think it was a bit harder than that, mind.
B: [laughs] That's the trick, isn't it. I had a client ring me in a right panic once, flooding all over his car park. It was a blocked grille. Bloke with a rake sorted it. I still wrote a report.
A: Yeah, exactly.
B: Is it all nights?
A: Rotating. Twelves. I do a lot of overtime, so it's fifty-odd hours most weeks. Pays alright for it. I want to get into network engineering though, days, proper money. Doing a CCNA, sort of.
B: Sort of?
A: Half doing it. Hard after a twelve-hour shift.
B: Fair. I did my chartership through work and the evenings were grim, I remember that. What do you do when you're not working?
A: Build PCs, mostly. Buy broken stuff off Marketplace, fix it, sell it on. Got a graphics card last week for like half what it should've been. Bloke didn't know what he had.
B: Is it actually broken?
A: Fan was dead. Fiver for a new one. I'll sell it for about two-fifty.
B: That's not bad at all. My son's nine, he's on at me for a gaming PC. I wouldn't know where to start.
A: Don't buy a prebuilt, they're a rip-off. Get one built, honestly, you'd save a couple hundred easy.
B: Is that you offering?
A: [laughs] Could do. Walsall's a bit far for you, though.
B: Bit, yeah. Do you follow the football at all?
A: Walsall. Loosely. They drew again Saturday.
B: Charlton for me. It's always the hope that kills you.
A: We don't have much hope, to be honest.
B: That's probably healthier.
A: Yeah.
B: How are you finding all this anyway, the study?
A: Alright. Puzzle bit was fine. Mainly here for the money, if I'm honest.
B: [laughs] At least you're honest about it. I think I'll probably—
